newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle H1 group net profit up 20 percent.
newsitem.headline: Nestle H1 group net profit up 20 percent.

text.p: International foods and beverage giant Nestle said net profit rose 20 percent in the first half of 1996 from the year-before period to 1.35 billion Swiss francs ($1.1 billion).
Nestle also forecast a favourable growth in sales and profit for the full year, but cautioned that net profit would not grow as fast in the second half as in the first six months.
The result nearly matched a consensus forecast among analysts for net profit of 1.36 billion Swiss francs.
Nestle said first half sales rose 5.6 percent to 28.44 billion Swiss francs, boosted by internal sales growth, a stronger dollar and weaker Swiss franc.

"For the full year 1996, Nestle expects the favourable trend in sales to continue, and consolidated sales for the year should approach 60 billion Swiss francs," it said in an interim report. 1995 sales totalled 56.48 billion swiss francs.
Nestle said net profits would not rise as fast in the second half because the first half rate was based in part on comparison with a weak start to 1995.
"For the whole of of 1996, net profit should grow at least at the same rate as consolidated sales," it said. ($ = 1.237 Swiss Francs)
